request: Analyze GSE179394 for PMID 34478753 (Diet and exercise reduce pre-existing NASH and fibrosis and have additional beneficial effects on the vasculature, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle via organ-crosstalk.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (STAR + HTSeq-count), liver, perigonadal WAT, quadriceps muscle
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 20 weeks of voluntary running-wheel exercise in obese Ldlr-/-.Leiden mice with pre-existing NASH that stay on HFD (HFD+running wheel vs HFD control), per organ (liver, eWAT, muscle)
final.sample_inclusion: all 50-week animals in the GEO series; organs analysed separately
planned_contrasts: H.Hrw vs H.H (exercise vs HFD control), per organ (abstract METHODS/RESULTS: treatment groups compared with untreated control group; paper DEG count not available)
H.Crw vs H.H (combination vs HFD control), per organ (abstract; count not available)
H.C vs H.H (diet change vs HFD control), per organ (abstract; count not available)
final.repeated_measure_unit: mouse (mousenr) appears in several organs, but organs are analysed separately, so each fit has one sample per mouse
final.paper_method: DESeq2 per GEO data_processing ('These counts serve as input for the statistical analysis using DEseq2 package'); exact model and threshold not available (abstract only)
final.paper_results: Abstract: pathway analysis shows exercise and diet change affect complementary metabolic/lipid-handling pathways and share inflammation pathways; no DEG counts or genes given

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: No full text available. Study map built from the PubMed abstract (METHODS, RESULTS) and the GEO series summary/overall_design/treatment_protocol. Groups: HFD 30 wk then 20 wk of HFD (control), HFD+running wheel (exercise), chow switch (diet), chow+running wheel (combination); chow reference kept on chow 50 wk. GEO donor.allergen.dose codes: C.C, H.H, H.Hrw, H.C, H.Crw (diet 1-30wk . diet 31-50wk, rw = running wheel). The 30-week reference groups in the paper are not in GEO.

checks: GEO series title equals the paper title
contact A. van den Hoek is the first author
138 matrix columns = 138 GEO samples after key normalisation

ownership.reasoning: GSE179394 series title and summary are the paper's title and abstract; the merged count file is the series-level supplementary file.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are the GEO titles without the leading 's' (liver/most eWAT) and, for 8 NovaSeq eWAT samples, with a '_R2' suffix; the 'R' suffix (e.g. 103566-001-028R) appears in both. Key derived from title by stripping 's'; matrix columns by stripping '_R2'. Exact match on the derived key, no positional alignment.

final.paper_input: HTSeq-count read counts, 'not normalised per sample', input to DESeq2 (GEO data_processing)

matrix.reasoning: integer fraction 1.0, max 2.4e6, median 0; GEO data_processing: STAR + HTSeq-count 0.6.1p1, raw counts for DESeq2.

candidates.value: pool runwheel Y vs N across diets
candidates.reason_rejected: mixes diet backgrounds (HFD and chow) and the chow reference; paper compares each intervention to the HFD control

candidates.value: pool all tissues in one model
candidates.reason_rejected: organs are distinct transcriptomes; the paper analyses each organ separately
diet-model reference contrast, not an exercise estimand

design.reasoning: Abstract: groups 'treated for 20 weeks with exercise, diet change or the combination' vs 'untreated (control group)'. Exercise effect as the paper intends = HHrw vs HH within each organ; combination vs HH also contains exercise; diet vs HH is kept as a paper contrast for context; HCrw vs HC (exercise on chow background) is exploratory and not stated in the abstract.

covariates.name: platform
covariates.disposition: included in the eWAT model only (NextSeq vs NovaSeq batch; liver all NextSeq, muscle all NovaSeq)

covariance.reasoning: eWAT samples were sequenced on two platforms (8 NovaSeq samples, all in HCrw and HHrw, re-sequenced '_R2'); HH, HC, CC eWAT are all NextSeq. Platform is partially confounded with exercise in eWAT, so it is included as a covariate in the eWAT fit (estimable within HCrw and HHrw). Liver and muscle are single-platform. Each mouse contributes one sample per organ, so no subject blocking.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), one model per organ

paper_route.reason: GEO data_processing names DESeq2; exact model unknown (abstract only)

deviations: platform covariate in eWAT is our decision; paper model unknown

method.reasoning: Raw HTSeq counts and GEO data_processing name DESeq2.

final.deviation_note: Full text unavailable; abstract states no threshold. Workflow default BH padj < 0.05 applied. Audit rule raw p < 0.01 is a labelled comparison only (commonly used by this group's DESeq2 pathway analyses; not verified against this paper).

caveats: Comparison with the paper rests on the abstract only; no paper DEG counts or genes available
eWAT exercise groups partly sequenced on a different platform; platform covariate added
Paper threshold unknown; workflow default applied

study.reasoning: Paper's contrasts (each intervention vs HFD control per organ) with the paper's method (DESeq2); threshold is the workflow default because the abstract states none.
